texts: good. both sides are bare plurals, so this lands on the prescribed opaque kind-level relation, with each compound's genus atom emitted alongside. Note that a kind relation deliberately does not distribute, so a question about one particular sky-cat stays unknown - that is the intended generic reading, not a loss.

bad: nothing at all was recorded for this sentence - 'nothing else' combines a negative-quantifier object with an exceptive ('else'), and neither has any carrier, so the entire diet restriction is absent from the knowledge base. Rewrite it as a self-contained exclusivity claim with an explicit subject and a stated object: 'Every sky-cat eats only nightmoths.' That gives a real eating event for 'only' to attach to instead of a bare negative quantifier. Be aware that the exhaustivity is then recorded as a marker rather than as an active exclusion, so it will not by itself rule other foods out.
good. the bare-plural generic becomes a per-cat distributing rule at 0.9/0.9, 'alone' sits in Manner where a how-adverb belongs, and the compound genus is emitted; nothing in the sentence is dropped.

bad: 'together' was slotted as a Manner adverb, which the adjudicator confirmed as a defect - on a per-cat rule it claims each individual sky-cat's own roosting is done together - and the compliant fix is simply to delete the word, so the collectivity is lost either way. Rewrite it as a kind-level relation between two bare plurals, the same shape that worked for the diet sentence: 'Sky-cats share roosts.' If you would rather keep the verb and the adverb, make the subject a definite set instead - 'The sky-cats roost together.' - which yields one group-level roosting event rather than a per-cat rule.

mixed: the count of twelve, the sky-cat group, the cliff-spires and the on-relation are all recorded and usable, but the verb 'roost' appears nowhere - a bare position clause with a postural verb mints no event, so the parse says only that each of the twelve is on the spires. If the roosting itself matters, give the clause a trigger that forces the event to be reified: 'A dozen sky-cats are roosting on the cliff-spires.' A time or frequency modifier ('...roost on the cliff-spires every night') does the same job while keeping the habitual reading, if the lore supplies one.

mixed: the denied group capability is handled correctly - both the group bundle and the per-member rule sit at strength 0.0, and 'exactly' is kept, so the claim is not widened to 'cannot count them at all' - but 'the Keepers' is read as an ordinary definite plural of the common noun, so the parse also asserts that each member is a 'keeper'. If that is what you mean, lowercase it to remove the doubt: 'The keepers cannot count the sky-cats exactly.' If the Keepers is instead the proper name of an order, a bare capitalized plural of the class word does not signal name-hood - extend the capitalized run beyond the bare class word, or state their kind in separate words, so the name and the kind are not the same token.

good. the definite plural distributes the property over its members rather than predicating it of the group as an object, and the intensifier rides along inside the same rule, so each spire is high and 'very' is not lost.
